signals.thesis: Compression can resolve into directional expansion when participation confirms release.
signals.trigger_logic: Squeeze is mature, breakout is present, and participation confirms expansion.
signals.invalidation_logic: Reject when release quality deteriorates, conviction fades, or execution readiness collapses rather than assuming every band break is tradable.
signals.execution_note: Use as a control breakout template, not just a default entry rule; promotion should favor pressure-aware and execution-gated variants.
signals.novelty_claim: Baseline control that combines compression and participation, but should be used as a quality anchor rather than a priority promotion path.

signals.thesis: A breakout is higher quality when latent pressure builds before visible expansion.
signals.trigger_logic: Latent pressure rises while compression persists, then release begins with improving conviction.
signals.invalidation_logic: Pressure dissipates without release or release becomes chaotic.
signals.execution_note: Prefer staged entry that combines pressure release with readiness quality rather than instant chase.
signals.novelty_claim: Combines latent pressure, squeeze maturity, and release quality to separate pre-break buildup from observed breakout alone.

signals.thesis: Some compressions are structurally fragile and should be filtered rather than traded as standard breakouts.
signals.trigger_logic: Compression exists but fragility score is low enough and release quality is acceptable.
signals.invalidation_logic: Fragility rises or expansion quality deteriorates immediately after break.
signals.execution_note: Best used as a breakout quality gate, not standalone trigger.
signals.novelty_claim: Differentiates tradable squeezes from disorderly ones.

signals.thesis: A breakout should be filtered through tape and execution quality before becoming tradeable.
signals.trigger_logic: Breakout aligns with supportive tape and execution readiness metrics.
signals.invalidation_logic: Tape support collapses or slippage hazard spikes.
signals.execution_note: Useful for routing signal candidates into strategy specs only when execution quality is acceptable.
signals.novelty_claim: Bridges breakout detection with execution state.

signals.thesis: Temporary displacement can revert when structure stays balanced and trend pressure remains weak.
signals.trigger_logic: Z-score enters stretch zone while regime remains balanced.
signals.invalidation_logic: Invalidate when directional coherence strengthens, tail persistence rises, or equilibrium drift keeps moving away from price rather than stabilizing.
signals.execution_note: Use as a baseline control and pair with tail persistence or drift context, not just isolated oversold/overbought thresholds.
signals.novelty_claim: Baseline control for equilibrium reversion; useful as a comparator, but differentiated promotion should favor drift-aware, tail-persistence, or shock-decay variants rather than raw z-score alone.

signals.thesis: Extended time spent in distribution tails can create a cleaner fade opportunity than one-off stretch.
signals.trigger_logic: Tail persistence is elevated but continuation quality is decaying.
signals.invalidation_logic: Tail persistence remains high with strengthening continuation.
signals.execution_note: Prefer partial entries only when persistence is tiring and recenter quality improves, rather than fading every extreme print.
signals.novelty_claim: Separates time-in-extreme persistence from one-off stretch and combines tail occupancy with decay quality rather than distance-only mean reversion.

signals.thesis: Reversion quality improves when displacement outruns a drifting equilibrium and then begins snapping back.
signals.trigger_logic: Drift gap is stretched and recenter velocity turns favorable.
signals.invalidation_logic: Equilibrium continues drifting away from price or snapback stalls.
signals.execution_note: Best when trend coherence is weak.
signals.novelty_claim: Separates static-mean reversion from drifting-equilibrium reversion.

signals.thesis: An abnormal impulse that quickly decays can create a high-quality shock reversal rather than ordinary recenter trade.
signals.trigger_logic: Impulse is abnormal, decay is visible, and continuation quality weakens.
signals.invalidation_logic: Shock extends into a genuine directional regime.
signals.execution_note: Should be tightly invalidated and not averaged into.
signals.novelty_claim: Targets abnormal impulse decay rather than generic overextension.

signals.thesis: Join an established trend when momentum realigns after prior alignment exists.
signals.trigger_logic: Momentum aligns with prevailing directional regime.
signals.invalidation_logic: Invalidate when momentum alignment weakens, trend coherence deteriorates, or execution readiness becomes hazardous rather than waiting for a simple cross reversal.
signals.execution_note: Use as a control continuation template, not just a standalone crossover trigger; promotion should favor coherence, pullback quality, and readiness filters.
signals.novelty_claim: Baseline control for continuation that combines momentum alignment with regime fit, but differentiated research should prefer pullback quality, reacceleration, and execution-readiness overlays rather than crossover logic alone.

signals.thesis: Not every pullback is equal; continuation improves when retrace quality remains structurally healthy.
signals.trigger_logic: Pullback stays shallow enough while trend anchors remain aligned.
signals.invalidation_logic: Retrace deepens into trend fragility.
signals.execution_note: Prefer entering on reclaim after healthy pullback.
signals.novelty_claim: Grades retrace health instead of treating all pullbacks alike.

signals.thesis: A mature trend can offer a better continuation entry when force reappears after orderly pause.
signals.trigger_logic: Trend coherence remains intact and reacceleration begins after pause.
signals.invalidation_logic: Pause becomes rollover or coherence breaks.
signals.execution_note: Promote only when orderly pause, renewed force, and execution readiness align as a quality-of-trend continuation event.
signals.novelty_claim: Combines pause quality, coherence, and directional renewal to capture trend continuation through reacceleration rather than generic momentum persistence.

signals.thesis: A continuation signal should only graduate when trend quality and execution quality align.
signals.trigger_logic: Continuation setup is valid and execution state remains supportive.
signals.invalidation_logic: Execution friction or slippage hazard rises beyond tolerance.
signals.execution_note: Acts as promotion filter from signal candidate to tradeable strategy.
signals.novelty_claim: Bridges trend logic with execution gating.

signals.thesis: Some of the best directional opportunities emerge when quiet conditions transition into orderly expansion.
signals.trigger_logic: Vol shift rises from quiet state with orderly release characteristics.
signals.invalidation_logic: Expansion becomes chaotic or fails to follow through.
signals.execution_note: Best combined with conviction filter.
signals.novelty_claim: Focuses on volatility state transition rather than static breakout only.

signals.thesis: Volatility bursts that are already exhausting can be faded more safely than fresh expansion.
signals.trigger_logic: Expansion is extended, exhaustion rises, and quality of follow-through decays.
signals.invalidation_logic: Burst reaccelerates into new directional regime.
signals.execution_note: Do not treat as standard mean reversion; this is a vol-state fade.
signals.novelty_claim: Targets exhausted expansion rather than simple overbought/oversold.

signals.thesis: Some low-vol trends hide instability and should trigger caution before continuation entries.
signals.trigger_logic: Trend is present but hidden fragility and volatility asymmetry worsen.
signals.invalidation_logic: Instability normalizes or trend quality improves.
signals.execution_note: Use as a warning/gating signal rather than direct entry.
signals.novelty_claim: Looks for hidden instability inside apparently orderly low-vol trends.

signals.thesis: Release from compression is only valuable when the release itself is orderly and persistent.
signals.trigger_logic: Compression release quality is strong and expansion persists.
signals.invalidation_logic: Release stalls or becomes disorderly.
signals.execution_note: Better as a breakout qualifier than a standalone thesis.
signals.novelty_claim: Grades release quality instead of assuming all breaks are equal.

signals.thesis: After transient execution stress, reentry becomes more attractive once spread and liquidity normalize.
signals.trigger_logic: Stress resolves and spread normalizes while directional thesis remains valid.
signals.invalidation_logic: Spread rewidens or liquidity recovery stalls.
signals.execution_note: Useful as a reentry filter after aborted first attempt.
signals.novelty_claim: Turns execution recovery into a signal layer object.

signals.thesis: Some apparently attractive entries are actually liquidity traps and should be explicitly avoided.
signals.trigger_logic: Directional setup exists but is blocked unless trap risk drops.
signals.invalidation_logic: Trap signal persists or adverse selection worsens.
signals.execution_note: Acts as veto layer for otherwise valid strategy candidates.
signals.novelty_claim: Avoidance-first signal built from microstructure risk.

signals.thesis: Short-lived aggressor imbalance with weak follow-through can create a snapback opportunity.
signals.trigger_logic: Aggressor flow becomes one-sided but tape impact decays rapidly.
signals.invalidation_logic: Imbalance persists with strengthening directional follow-through.
signals.execution_note: Best for short-horizon tactical entries only.
signals.novelty_claim: Microstructure snapback rather than bar-level mean reversion.

signals.thesis: A valid directional thesis should be aborted when execution hazard overwhelms expected edge.
signals.trigger_logic: Trade candidate exists but hazard metrics exceed tolerance.
signals.invalidation_logic: Hazard normalizes and tradeability returns.
signals.execution_note: This is a stop-go signal for promotion logic, not a direct market direction signal.
signals.novelty_claim: Explicit hazard-aware veto that combines slippage, friction, and tradeability risk rather than forcing direction-only signals into bad execution states.
